domains.name: Launcher desktop control center
domains.promise: The Electron launcher installs, onboards, runs, updates, and cleanly uninstalls the full SomniBot stack (bot, dashboard, migrations, and optional Lavalink/Valkey sidecars) on Windows and Linux, stores credentials encrypted via the OS keychain, prompts the operator before any update download, updates cleanly from the N-1 release to v1, and deploys to a new VPS only after showing the literal commands and receiving explicit operator approval, targeting dedicated somnibot-prefixed destinations and never touching existing Somni or Hermes installs.

controls.description: Updates are announced but never downloaded until the operator explicitly clicks Install now (electron-updater autoDownload=false, download starts only via the updater:download IPC call).

constraints.reason: Owner decision: updates always prompt before download; silent downloads are never permitted.

controls.description: When an update has been downloaded and staged, install it automatically on next app quit/relaunch (electron-updater autoInstallOnAppQuit).
Where the stack runs: regular-local keeps bot and dashboard on this machine (public callbacks optionally via Tailscale Funnel); vps switches to the guided VPS deployment path with an HTTPS domain.
Whether the launcher manages a bundled Lavalink music sidecar process alongside bot and dashboard.

Absolute remote directory the VPS deployment operates in. Must be a dedicated somnibot-prefixed destination (final path segment starts with somnibot-); paths pointing at existing Somni or Hermes installations are rejected outright.

Require OS keychain (DPAPI/libsecret) encryption for sensitive credentials at rest. When the keychain is unavailable, the launcher must warn prominently and obtain explicit operator acknowledgment before storing anything in plaintext.
Route store payments through the PayPal sandbox environment instead of live PayPal.

The owner-facing brand name shown on launcher surfaces (window title, update prompts, log pane). White-label: the owner's brand leads everywhere, with only a subtle powered-by-SomniBot attribution line.

defaults.rationale: Owner decision: the operator always approves before any bytes download; matches autoDownload=false in updater.ts.
A staged update the operator already approved should complete on next launch without re-asking; matches autoInstallOnAppQuit=true.
Out of the box the stack runs entirely on the operator's machine; VPS mode is an explicit opt-in guided flow (config-store DEFAULTS.runtimeMode).
Music sidecar is opt-in so first run stays light; matches DEFAULTS.lavalinkEnabled=false.
No remote destination exists until the operator supplies one; an empty path blocks the deployment plan rather than guessing a directory.
Owner decision: secure credential storage is the default; plaintext at rest only ever happens after a loud warning and explicit operator acknowledgment.
Guardrail: fresh installs must not accidentally take live money; matches DEFAULTS.paypalSandbox=true.
Ships with the product name until the owner sets their own brand during guided onboarding; every surface then re-renders under the owner's brand.

permissions.actor: Desktop operator (the local user who installed the launcher)
permissions.action: Start and stop the bundled bot, dashboard, migrations, and sidecar processes
permissions.enforcement: Only the launcher's own renderer can invoke main-process actions through the contextBridge preload IPC allowlist; no remote surface can drive the stack.

permissions.action: Download an update without an explicit operator prompt
permissions.enforcement: autoDownload=false in the main process; downloads begin only when the renderer sends updater:download after the operator accepts the prompt.

permissions.action: Execute a remote-changing VPS command without the main-process approval dialog
permissions.enforcement: confirmVpsDeploymentApproval gates every command flagged changesRemote/approvalRequired behind a native warning dialog listing the literal redacted commands; cancel means zero remote commands run.

permissions.actor: Dashboard renderer and spawned child processes
permissions.action: Read raw credential store contents or decrypted secrets outside the injected environment
permissions.enforcement: Sensitive fields are safeStorage-encrypted at rest; only the main process decrypts and injects them into child process environments, and VPS plan output shows secrets as redacted markers only.

messages.trigger: electron-updater reports update-available after a launch or manual check
messages.defaultTemplate: A fresh {brand-name} update ({version}) is ready when you are. Nothing downloads until you hit Install now.

messages.trigger: Update download completed and staged for install
messages.defaultTemplate: Update {version} is staged. Restart {brand-name} whenever it suits you and the new version takes over from there.
The update check hit a snag: {error-message}. Your current install keeps running; try again from the launcher menu whenever you like.

messages.trigger: First run of an unsigned build on Windows
messages.surface: Launcher first-run guidance panel and download page
messages.defaultTemplate: Windows SmartScreen may warn because this build is unsigned. Verify the SHA-256 checksum {checksum} against the download page, then choose More info and Run anyway.

messages.trigger: OS keychain (safeStorage) is unavailable when saving credentials
messages.defaultTemplate: No OS keychain was found, so {brand-name} cannot encrypt your credentials at rest. Install a keyring (gnome-keyring, kwallet, or KeePassXC) and try again, or explicitly acknowledge plaintext storage.

messages.trigger: Operator requests a VPS deployment and the plan is ready
messages.defaultTemplate: Review the exact commands below before anything touches {ssh-target}. Only the dedicated somnibot-scoped path {deploy-path} will be modified, and nothing runs until you approve.

messages.trigger: Deployment path fails safety or destination checks
messages.defaultTemplate: That deploy path was rejected: {reason}. The launcher only deploys into dedicated somnibot-prefixed directories and never touches existing Somni or Hermes installs.

messages.trigger: An approved remote command exited non-zero or a health probe failed
messages.defaultTemplate: Deployment stopped at {command-label}: {error-message}. Nothing after it ran; review the log and the rollback plan before retrying.

messages.trigger: A managed child process (bot, dashboard, Lavalink, Valkey) exited unexpectedly
messages.surface: Launcher status panel and log pane
messages.defaultTemplate: The {process-name} process stopped unexpectedly. {brand-name} is bringing it back; full details are in the launcher console.

values.description: Launcher installed; guided first-run onboarding not yet complete, normal stack access blocked until it is (firstRunComplete=false).
Credentials validated and saved encrypted; onboarding complete; stack not currently running.
Bot, dashboard, and enabled sidecars are running as launcher-managed child processes; migrations applied.
An operator-approved update has downloaded and is staged (updateReady=true) awaiting restart.
A VPS deployment plan is rendered with the literal command list and redacted env file, awaiting the operator's approval dialog decision.
Approved commands completed against the somnibot-scoped deploy path and public health probes verified the stack.
A child process crashed or a remote deployment step failed; the launcher surfaces the failure and offers recovery.
OS uninstaller removed the app cleanly; reinstall yields a working launcher again.

transitions.trigger: Operator finishes the guided first-run setup and credentials validate
transitions.expectedEffect: firstRunComplete flips true; sensitive fields are keychain-encrypted into the config store; owner brand name applied to launcher surfaces.

transitions.trigger: Operator clicks Start
transitions.expectedEffect: Main process runs pending database migrations, then spawns bot and dashboard (plus Lavalink/Valkey when enabled) with env built from the encrypted store; PIDs recorded in lastPids.

transitions.trigger: Operator clicks Stop or quits the launcher
transitions.expectedEffect: All managed child processes terminate; lastPids cleared so no orphans remain.

transitions.trigger: Operator accepts the update prompt and the download completes
transitions.expectedEffect: updateReady=true, updater:downloaded broadcast; the running stack is untouched until restart.

transitions.trigger: Operator clicks Restart (updater:install)
transitions.expectedEffect: quitAndInstall relaunches on the new version with credentials, guild list, and runtime settings intact; N-1 to v1 upgrades preserve all state.

transitions.trigger: Operator requests VPS deployment with vps runtime mode and valid networking config
transitions.expectedEffect: buildVpsDeploymentPlan renders the literal command list, redacted env file, service layout, approval gates, and rollback plan; secrets shown only as redacted markers.

transitions.trigger: Operator approves the main-process confirmation dialog
transitions.expectedEffect: Approved commands run in declared order against the somnibot-prefixed deploy path only; env file chmod 0600; health probes must return healthy before deployment is declared complete.

transitions.trigger: Operator cancels the confirmation dialog
transitions.expectedEffect: Zero remote commands execute; the plan is discarded with no side effects on the VPS.

transitions.trigger: A managed child process exits unexpectedly or a dependency check fails
transitions.expectedEffect: Failure logged and surfaced in the status panel; automatic respawn attempted; credentials never appear in logs.

transitions.trigger: Automatic respawn succeeds or the operator restarts the failed component
transitions.expectedEffect: Stack returns to healthy with no duplicate processes and no lost configuration.

transitions.trigger: Operator runs the OS uninstaller
transitions.expectedEffect: App binaries and shortcuts are removed cleanly; a subsequent reinstall produces a working launcher that can re-read or freshly re-create configuration.

failures.trigger: GitHub releases feed is unreachable or the update download is interrupted
failures.expectedBehavior: The current version keeps running untouched; updater:error is broadcast to the banner; no partially-applied update exists on disk; startup is never blocked by a failed background check.

failures.trigger: safeStorage reports encryption unavailable (e.g. Linux without a keyring daemon) while saving credentials
failures.expectedBehavior: The launcher warns prominently on the credentials surface and refuses silent plaintext persistence; secrets are stored unencrypted only after explicit operator acknowledgment, and the warning names the keyring packages that fix it.

failures.trigger: Deploy path is relative, contains traversal or unsafe characters, lacks the somnibot- destination prefix, or points at an existing Somni or Hermes installation
failures.expectedBehavior: The plan is returned blocked with explicit human-readable reasons; canApprove=false; no SSH command of any kind executes, including read-only preflight.

failures.trigger: An approved remote command exits non-zero, times out (45-minute build ceiling), or a health probe does not return healthy
failures.expectedBehavior: Execution halts at the failed step; no subsequent commands run; the failure with its redacted command line is logged; the rollback plan (fetch, checkout known-good, rebuild, health verify) is offered but never auto-executed.

failures.trigger: Bot, dashboard, Lavalink, or Valkey child process exits unexpectedly while the stack is running
failures.expectedBehavior: Crash is logged with the process name, an automatic respawn is attempted with backoff, the status panel shows degraded health, and no secret material is emitted to logs.

evidence.observer: E2E Discord client in the run-prefixed test guild watching the bot launched by the launcher
evidence.expectedObservation: After launcher Start, the bot comes online in the test guild and answers a smoke slash command; after Stop it goes offline with no zombie presence.

evidence.observer: Supabase probes using service-role and anon clients against tables touched by launcher-run migrations
evidence.expectedObservation: Migrations applied by the launcher leave RLS enabled on guild-scoped tables; the anon client cannot read another guild's configuration rows created during the run.

evidence.observer: Audit-log query over launcher lifecycle events
evidence.expectedObservation: Update staged/installed, VPS plan blocked/approved/executed, and crash events each produce durable audit rows that are never deleted, only anonymized under retention.

evidence.observer: Owner notification sink (launcher status surface plus configured owner channel)
evidence.expectedObservation: Keychain-unavailable, VPS command failure, and child-process crash each raise an owner-visible notice; routine successes do not spam the owner.

evidence.observer: Launcher UI text capture across window title, updater banner, and VPS dialogs
evidence.expectedObservation: All operator-facing copy leads with the configured owner brand name and carries only a subtle powered-by-SomniBot attribution.

evidence.observer: Harness replaying updater:install IPC and re-running the approved VPS command list
evidence.expectedObservation: Replayed install requests and re-executed idempotent deployment steps (chmod, compose up) produce no duplicate installs, duplicate containers, or repeated side effects.

evidence.observer: Post-run sweep of run-prefixed launcher artifacts
evidence.expectedObservation: Temp session-token directories, run-prefixed test deploy directories, and staged test update artifacts are removed; only durable audit rows remain.

scenarios.promise: A fresh install walks the operator through guided onboarding before any normal access, then starts the full bundled stack (migrations, bot, dashboard) with safe defaults: regular-local mode, PayPal sandbox, Lavalink off, prompt-before-download updates, keychain-encrypted credentials.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Onboarding gates access until credentials validate; Start applies migrations then brings bot and dashboard up; the updater checks but downloads nothing without a prompt; config file on disk holds only encrypted secret values.

assertions.expectedObservation: The launcher-spawned bot appears online in the run-prefixed test guild and answers a smoke slash command.
Launcher-applied migrations complete and RLS still denies anon reads of guild-scoped rows.
Onboarding completion and first stack start are recorded as audit events.
No failure notifications fire during a clean default run.
First-run surfaces show the default brand with subtle powered-by-SomniBot attribution, ready for owner rebrand.
Clicking Start twice in the default flow yields exactly one stack instance.
The run's temp token directory and test config artifacts are removed after teardown.

scenarios.promise: Configuring lavalink-enabled=true and runtime-mode=vps with a valid somnibot-prefixed deploy path takes effect: the Lavalink sidecar is managed and the VPS plan renders the literal command list for review.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Lavalink starts and stops under launcher management; the deployment plan reaches status ready with the exact redacted command lines, 0600 env-file requirement, approval gates, and rollback plan visible before anything runs.

assertions.expectedObservation: With Lavalink managed, a music smoke command in the test guild reports the audio node reachable.
Runtime-mode and sidecar settings persist in the operator's scope only; anon clients cannot read them.
The config change and plan-ready events are audited with the redacted target.
Plan readiness is surfaced to the operator; no failure notice fires.
The VPS approval dialog copy carries the owner brand voice.
Requesting the plan twice renders identical commands without executing anything remotely.
Run-prefixed plan artifacts are deleted after the run.

scenarios.promise: A different configuration also takes effect: a custom owner-brand-name re-renders launcher surfaces, and with the operator declining the update prompt nothing downloads while auto-install-on-quit=false keeps a previously staged update from applying on quit.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: All updater and status copy shows the custom brand; declining the prompt results in zero download traffic; quitting does not install the staged test update when auto-install is disabled.

assertions.expectedObservation: Bot-side surfaces driven by launcher config show the custom brand in the test guild.
The brand setting is readable only within the owner's scope under RLS.
The declined update prompt is audited as operator-declined, not as an error.
No notification fires for a declined optional update.
Updater banner and window title render the custom brand with subtle attribution intact.
Re-sending the decline produces no download and no duplicate prompt records.
The staged test update artifact is removed during teardown.

scenarios.promise: Invalid configuration is rejected atomically: a relative or traversal-laden deploy path, a VPS domain carrying an explicit port, or a non-somnibot destination each block the plan with explicit reasons and persist nothing as deploy-ready.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: buildVpsDeploymentPlan returns status blocked with human-readable blockedReasons, canApprove=false, empty command list; the previous valid configuration remains untouched and no SSH connection is attempted.

assertions.expectedObservation: The running bot in the test guild is unaffected by the rejected configuration attempt.
No partially-saved deploy configuration row exists after rejection.
The blocked plan is audited as launcher.vps_plan_blocked with the reason category.
The rejection is shown inline to the operator; no escalation notice fires.
The rejection copy uses the owner-branded voice and names the somnibot-prefix rule plainly.
Submitting the same invalid path repeatedly produces the same rejection with no state drift.
No leftover blocked-plan artifacts persist after the run.

scenarios.promise: Nothing bypasses the operator: a renderer-forged request to execute VPS deployment without the main-process approval dialog is denied, and child processes cannot read raw credential store contents.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The deployment executor refuses to run any changesRemote command without an operatorApproved decision from the native dialog; the config file on disk yields only ciphertext for sensitive keys; the preload bridge exposes no raw-secret channel.

assertions.expectedObservation: No deployment side effects are observable from the test guild after the denied attempt.
No deployment or credential rows were written by the unauthorized path.
The denied unapproved execution attempt is recorded in the audit trail.
The operator is notified that an unapproved execution attempt was blocked.
The denial message is rendered in the owner-branded voice.
Repeated forged requests are each denied with no cumulative effect.
No artifacts from the denied attempt persist beyond audit rows.

scenarios.promise: Dependency failures fail safe: an unreachable update feed never blocks startup or corrupts the install, and a missing OS keychain never silently downgrades credential storage to plaintext.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With the feed unreachable the launcher starts normally, shows the branded update-error banner, and the current version keeps running; with safeStorage unavailable the credentials form warns loudly and requires explicit acknowledgment before any plaintext write.

assertions.expectedObservation: The bot still starts and serves the test guild while the update feed is down.
No credential material lands in the database during the keychain-failure path.
launcher.update_failed and launcher.keychain_unavailable events are both recorded.
The keychain warning reaches the operator prominently; the feed failure stays a quiet banner.
Both failure messages use the owner-branded templates with actionable next steps.
Repeated failed checks do not stack banners or partially-downloaded update files.
No partial download artifacts remain after the failed update attempts.

scenarios.promise: Transient failures converge on retry: a temporarily failing SSH preflight or interrupted update download succeeds on the next attempt without duplicated side effects.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The read-only preflight retried after a transient network fault reports ready exactly once; a resumed update download stages a single valid update; no remote mutation occurred during any failed attempt.

assertions.expectedObservation: The test-guild bot remains stable across the retry cycle.
Retry attempts add no duplicate configuration or deployment rows.
Each attempt is audited distinctly, showing failure then converged success.
Only a persistent failure would notify; a converged retry stays quiet.
Interim retry messaging keeps the branded, reassuring tone.
The converged state equals a single successful attempt, byte for byte on the staged update.
Failed-attempt temp files are cleaned up alongside run artifacts.

scenarios.promise: Replay is harmless: re-sending updater:install after installation, and re-running the approved idempotent deployment command list, cause no double-install, duplicate containers, or repeated remote mutations.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: A second updater:install with no staged update is a no-op; re-executing chmod 0600 and docker compose up -d against the same somnibot-scoped path converges to the identical healthy stack with no new side effects.

assertions.expectedObservation: Exactly one bot presence exists in the test guild after replayed operations.
Replayed operations write no duplicate rows.
Replays are audited as no-op or converged events, preserving the original record.
Replays trigger no duplicate notifications.
Any replay-facing message stays branded and calm rather than alarming.
Container list, env file mode, and installed version are identical before and after the replay.
Replay testing leaves no extra artifacts beyond the original run set.

scenarios.promise: State survives restart: after killing and relaunching the launcher (including the N-1 to v1 upgrade path), credentials decrypt, guild entries persist, a staged update still applies, and stale PIDs are reconciled without orphan processes.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Relaunch restores the configured state from the encrypted store; lastPids from the previous run are detected and cleaned; the staged update installs on the restart path; a launcher updated from the previous release keeps every setting.

assertions.expectedObservation: After restart the bot reconnects to the test guild with the same configuration.
Persisted Supabase state from before the restart is intact and still RLS-protected.
Restart, stale-PID cleanup, and update-applied events appear in order in the audit trail.
The operator sees a clean-restart status rather than failure noise.
The owner's brand settings survive the restart and upgrade unchanged.
The relaunch spawns exactly one instance of each managed process.
Orphan processes from the killed run are terminated and their temp files removed.

scenarios.promise: Concurrent actions are safe: double-clicking Start, or racing two VPS approval dialogs, results in exactly one stack instance and at most one deployment execution.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Process-manager guards collapse simultaneous start requests into one spawn per service; the second approval attempt while a deployment is executing is refused; no interleaved remote command streams occur.

assertions.expectedObservation: A single bot session serves the test guild despite the racing start requests.
Concurrent operations produce no duplicate or conflicting configuration rows.
The audit trail shows one accepted action and one explicitly-refused concurrent action.
The refused concurrent deployment attempt is surfaced to the operator.
The busy-state refusal message keeps the branded voice.
The end state is identical to a single serial execution of the winning action.
The losing racer leaves no half-started processes or files behind.

scenarios.promise: Multi-guild entries are isolated: disabling the second run-prefixed guild in the launcher guild list changes only that guild; the bot receives the enabled-guild set and guild A behavior is untouched.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With two guild entries, toggling guild B's enabled flag removes only guild B from the DISCORD_GUILD_ID set passed to the bot; guild A commands, config, and data remain fully functional and invisible to guild B.

assertions.expectedObservation: Guild A still answers commands while guild B stops receiving service after being disabled.
Guild-scoped rows for A and B remain mutually unreadable across guild contexts.
The guild-entry toggle is audited with the specific guild id affected.
The operator sees which guild was disabled; guild A raises no alerts.
Each guild's surfaces keep their own branding configuration independently.
Re-applying the same toggle is a no-op with no cross-guild bleed.
Both run-prefixed test guild entries and their artifacts are removed at teardown.

scenarios.promise: Every run-prefixed launcher resource is cleaned: temp session-token directories, test deploy directories under the somnibot- prefix, staged test updates, and test guild entries are removed while audit history stays durable.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: A post-run sweep finds zero run-prefixed files, directories, processes, or remote test paths; audit rows describing the run remain readable and are never deleted.

assertions.expectedObservation: No run-prefixed channels, messages, or bot artifacts remain in the test guild.
Run-prefixed database rows are removed or anonymized; RLS posture is unchanged.
Audit rows for the run persist after cleanup, satisfying anonymize-over-delete.
A cleanup summary is available to the operator without alert noise.
Cleanup does not disturb the owner's branding configuration.
Running cleanup twice is safe and finds nothing on the second pass.
The sweep report lists every created resource matched to a deletion or anonymization.

domains.name: License SDK and validation API
domains.promise: The @somnibot/license-sdk and the dashboard license API validate license keys for real-store products against hashed key storage, enforce per-product device limits through atomic session registration, keep sessions honest with heartbeats, honor a bounded offline grace window on a monotonic clock without ever extending a lapsed payment-grace deadline, and give the owner and the customer working recovery resets that free device slots — all strictly guild-scoped and replay-safe. License access is account-bound commerce state and never touches the play-money game economy.

controls.description: Per-product license delivery mode string (dashboard PUT /api/license/config/[productId], max 32 chars); portal_only is the canonical shipped mode where keys are surfaced through the customer portal.
Maximum concurrent active device sessions per license key; enforced atomically by the license_validate_device RPC at validation time.
Server-directed heartbeat cadence returned to the SDK on validation; the SDK clamps any interval below 30 seconds up to 30 to protect the API.
How long a device may keep operating on its cached validation while the license server is unreachable, measured on a server-time-anchored monotonic clock.
Whether validation requires the bound customer to still be a member of the product's Discord guild.
Per-product feature flag strings delivered to the SDK on successful validation for in-app gating.
How long the SDK serves a cached valid response before revalidating; always capped at a payment-grace deadline when one is in force.

defaults.rationale: Keys are account-bound and reached through the branded customer portal by default; matches the route-level default in /api/license/config.
Three devices covers a customer's desktop, laptop, and spare without inviting key sharing; matches the API default.
Five-minute heartbeats keep session truth fresh without meaningful API load; matches the API default.
A 24-hour offline window is member-respectful for flaky connections while the server-side heartbeat system remains the authoritative enforcement.
Products are community goods; leaving the guild ends entitlement checks by default, and owners can relax this per product.
No flags until the owner defines them; the SDK receives an empty list rather than an absent field.
One minute of client caching absorbs bursts while keeping revocations fast; matches the SDK constructor default.

permissions.actor: Any external app presenting a license key
permissions.enforcement: Public endpoints protected by per-IP and per-key-hash rate limits; keys are stored and compared only as SHA-256 hashes; every attempt is logged to license_validations.

permissions.action: List device sessions (GET /api/license/sessions) and revoke one (DELETE /api/license/sessions/[id]) as a recovery reset
permissions.enforcement: requireGuildOwner plus a parent license_keys.guild_id ownership check on every session operation; revocation marks the session inactive with reason admin_revoked.

permissions.action: Read, enumerate, or revoke another guild's license keys, sessions, or customer PII
permissions.enforcement: All admin lookups are constrained to the caller's guild_id (V47-C2); cross-guild UUID or hash guesses return not-found, never data.

permissions.actor: Customer holding a valid portal token
permissions.action: View their own license keys and device sessions, and free a device slot from the portal
permissions.enforcement: x-portal-token is hash-matched against unexpired, unrevoked portal_sessions and rate limited; data is filtered to the token's customer_id only.

messages.trigger: License validates successfully for a device
messages.surface: Customer app via SDK response and portal license card
messages.defaultTemplate: Welcome back, {customer-name}! Your {product-name} license is active on this device.

messages.trigger: Validation from a new device fingerprint would exceed max-devices
messages.defaultTemplate: This key is already active on {active-devices} of {max-devices} allowed devices. Free a slot from your portal, or ask {owner-brand} support for a reset.

messages.trigger: Validation or heartbeat reports status grace_period after a payment failure
messages.surface: Customer app via SDK response and portal banner
messages.defaultTemplate: Your payment for {product-name} needs attention. Access continues until {grace-ends-at}; update your payment method to keep everything running.

messages.trigger: Key is revoked, expired, or its payment grace lapsed
messages.defaultTemplate: This license for {product-name} is no longer valid. If that seems wrong, contact {owner-brand} support with your order id.

messages.trigger: License server unreachable while a cached validation is still within the offline window
messages.defaultTemplate: We cannot reach the license server right now, so you are covered by the offline window until {offline-until}. The app revalidates automatically once you are back online.

messages.trigger: A device session is revoked by the owner or freed by the customer as a recovery reset
messages.surface: Dashboard licenses page and customer portal
messages.defaultTemplate: Device {device-name} was signed out of your {product-name} license. That slot is free again.

messages.trigger: First-time validation fails with no cached result, or the composite lookup RPC errors
messages.defaultTemplate: The license server for {product-name} is unreachable and this device has no prior validation to fall back on. Check your connection and try again.

messages.trigger: Per-IP or per-key rate limit trips on the validation API
messages.defaultTemplate: Too many license checks in a short burst. The server asked us to wait {retry-after-seconds} seconds before trying again.

values.description: Device holds a key but no accepted validation or active session.
Server accepted the validation; a device session row is active and heartbeats run at the directed interval.
Server unreachable; the SDK serves the cached validation within the offline window on the anchored monotonic clock.
Payment failed; the license stays valid until grace_period_ends_at, with the SDK cache hard-capped at that deadline.
Key rejected: revoked, expired, grace lapsed, or offline window exhausted; heartbeats stopped and cache cleared.
This device's session was ended (SDK deactivate or recovery reset); the device slot is free for reuse.

transitions.trigger: POST /api/license/validate with a valid key, product, and registrable device fingerprint
transitions.expectedEffect: Atomic device registration within max-devices; session id issued; features, tier, and heartbeat interval returned; SDK auto-starts heartbeats.

transitions.trigger: Periodic POST /api/license/heartbeat with the session id
transitions.expectedEffect: last_seen_at refreshed and the next interval returned; the server time anchor is re-established on the SDK.

transitions.trigger: Network failure on a validate or heartbeat call within the offline window
transitions.expectedEffect: SDK serves the cached result with status offline_grace, timed on the monotonic clock so wall-clock manipulation cannot stretch the window.

transitions.trigger: Connectivity restored and revalidation succeeds
transitions.expectedEffect: Fresh server response replaces the cache and re-anchors server time; the session continues without a new device slot.

transitions.trigger: Offline elapsed time exceeds offline-grace-period-seconds
transitions.expectedEffect: Cache cleared, heartbeats stopped, SDK reports offline_grace_expired; no zombie session is asserted.

transitions.trigger: Validation or heartbeat reports status grace_period with grace_period_ends_at
transitions.expectedEffect: SDK caps its cache at the anchored deadline, records the offline hard stop, and surfaces the branded payment warning.

transitions.trigger: A later heartbeat reports a healthy non-grace status after payment recovery
transitions.expectedEffect: Cached payload is reconciled back to active and the stale grace deadline is dropped so the customer is immediately unrestricted.

transitions.trigger: grace_period_ends_at passes, whether the device is online or offline
transitions.expectedEffect: The server rejects the key and the SDK hard-stops at the deadline even mid-offline-window; heartbeats cease.

transitions.trigger: SDK deactivate() on uninstall, or an owner/customer recovery reset revokes the session
transitions.expectedEffect: Session marked inactive with its deactivation reason; the device slot is freed and the reset confirmation is surfaced.

transitions.trigger: A fresh validation from the same or a replacement device
transitions.expectedEffect: The freed slot is occupied by exactly one new session; recovery is complete without owner-side key regeneration.

transitions.trigger: Guild owner revokes the key or session from the dashboard
transitions.expectedEffect: The very next validation or heartbeat for that device is rejected; the customer sees the branded revocation message with the support path.

failures.trigger: License server unreachable on a device with no cached successful validation
failures.expectedBehavior: SDK returns valid:false with status network_error and asserts no entitlement; no offline grace applies because there is nothing trustworthy to fall back on.

failures.trigger: Validation from a new fingerprint when max-devices sessions are already active
failures.expectedBehavior: Validation is rejected without creating a session; the attempt is logged to license_validations; the customer is pointed at the portal reset path rather than silently evicting another device.

failures.trigger: The cached payment-grace deadline passes while the device is offline inside its offline window
failures.expectedBehavior: The SDK hard-stops at the anchored deadline instead of riding out the longer offline window; cache is cleared and heartbeats stop, so going offline cannot keep a lapsed payment valid.

failures.trigger: Per-IP or per-key rate limit exceeded on the validation API
failures.expectedBehavior: 429 with a Retry-After header; key status and sessions are unchanged; the SDK backs off and retries after the stated delay without hammering.

failures.trigger: The composite license_validate_lookup RPC errors server-side
failures.expectedBehavior: The API fails closed with a 500 and valid:false, writes no partial session state, and logs the internal error without leaking key material or internals to the caller.

evidence.observer: E2E Discord client observing the run-prefixed test guild during license lifecycle runs
evidence.expectedObservation: Guild-membership-gated validations reflect real membership changes in the test guild, and license activity never mints game currency or any game-economy artifact in Discord.

evidence.observer: Supabase probes as anon, cross-guild owner, and service-role against license_keys, license_sessions, and license_validations
evidence.expectedObservation: Keys exist only as SHA-256 hashes; anon and cross-guild clients cannot read keys, sessions, or customer PII; service paths stay guild-scoped.

evidence.observer: Query over license_validations and audit rows for the run's keys
evidence.expectedObservation: Every validation attempt (success, invalid key, device-limit rejection, rate limit) leaves a durable log row with IP and result; rows are never deleted, only anonymized under retention.

evidence.observer: Owner notification sink for license health events
evidence.expectedObservation: Grace lapses and server-side lookup failures notify the owner; routine validations and customer-side rate limits do not.

evidence.observer: Capture of SDK-surfaced message templates and portal license pages
evidence.expectedObservation: Customer-facing license copy leads with the owner's brand and support path, with only subtle powered-by-SomniBot attribution on portal surfaces.

evidence.observer: Harness replaying identical validate, heartbeat, and deactivate requests
evidence.expectedObservation: Replays create no duplicate sessions, consume no extra device slots, flip no key status twice, and grant nothing beyond the single original entitlement.

evidence.observer: Post-run sweep of run-prefixed customers, products, keys, and sessions
evidence.expectedObservation: All run-prefixed license fixtures are removed or anonymized; validation-log audit rows persist per anonymize-over-delete.

scenarios.promise: Out of the box (portal_only, 3 devices, 300s heartbeat, 24h offline grace, guild membership required), a customer's app validates its key, receives features and a session, heartbeats on schedule, and deactivates cleanly on uninstall.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: validate() returns valid with session id, tier, and features; heartbeats at the directed 300s cadence keep the session fresh; deactivate() frees the device slot; all attempts appear in license_validations.

assertions.expectedObservation: The bound customer's test-guild membership satisfies the default membership requirement.
The created session row is reachable only through guild-scoped owner queries, never anonymously.
The validation and deactivation both leave durable log rows with results and IP.
A healthy default lifecycle raises no owner alerts.
The success message greets the customer under the owner's brand.
The same device validating twice reuses one session and one device slot.
The run-prefixed key, customer, and session are swept after the run.

scenarios.promise: Dashboard config takes effect: setting max_devices=1 and heartbeat_interval_seconds=60 for the product means a second device is rejected at the limit and the SDK heartbeats at the new 60-second cadence.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: PUT /api/license/config/[productId] persists; device one validates, device two is refused with the device-limit message; observed heartbeat spacing follows the 60s server-directed interval.

assertions.expectedObservation: The rejected second device causes no change to the customer's guild roles or access.
The product config row is writable only by the owning guild's owner.
The config change and the device_limit rejection are both logged.
The owner can see the limit rejection in the dashboard without alert spam.
The limit message names the owner brand and the portal reset path.
Re-submitting the identical config PUT is an idempotent upsert.
The tightened test config is removed with its run-prefixed product.

scenarios.promise: A second distinct configuration also takes effect: max_devices=5, offline_grace_period_seconds=3600, feature_flags and tier set — five devices coexist, the offline window shortens to one hour, and the SDK receives the flags and tier.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Five fingerprints hold concurrent sessions; a sixth is refused; a device offline past one hour reports offline_grace_expired instead of the default 24h; getFeatures() and getTier() return the configured values.

assertions.expectedObservation: Feature-flagged behavior in the test guild follows the configured flags for entitled customers.
All five session rows stay scoped to the owning guild and customer.
The five activations and the sixth rejection are individually logged.
No alert fires for expected limit enforcement.
Portal license cards show the configured tier under the owner's brand.
Re-validating each of the five devices adds no sixth session.
All five run-prefixed sessions are swept at teardown.

scenarios.promise: Invalid product license config is rejected and rolled back: max_devices=0, a negative heartbeat interval, an offline grace beyond seven days, or an over-length mode string are all refused by validation with the stored config unchanged.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Each invalid PUT returns a 4xx validation error naming the offending field; a follow-up GET shows the prior config intact; running SDK sessions are unaffected.

assertions.expectedObservation: Entitled customers in the test guild see no interruption during the rejected config attempts.
No partial or invalid config row is persisted.
The rejected attempts are recorded with their validation failure reasons.
The owner sees the inline validation error, not an escalation.
Validation errors are phrased in the branded, actionable voice.
Repeating the invalid PUT produces the same rejection with zero state drift.
No rejected-config residue survives the run.

scenarios.promise: Permission boundaries hold: an unrelated guild's owner cannot read or revoke this guild's keys or sessions (not-found, never data), and portal requests without a valid token get 401 with nothing leaked.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Cross-guild GET /api/license-keys/[key], GET /api/license/sessions, and DELETE /api/license/sessions/[id] all return not-found despite valid UUIDs; /api/portal/licenses without x-portal-token returns 401; no customer PII crosses the boundary.

assertions.expectedObservation: The foreign owner's attempts cause no visible effect in either test guild.
Direct table probes as the foreign owner return zero rows for this guild's license data.
The denied cross-guild attempts are recorded in the audit trail.
The legitimate owner is not disrupted; repeated probing is surfaceable as suspicious activity.
Denial responses are generic and unbranded-internally, leaking no key or customer detail.
Repeated denied attempts accumulate no partial state.
Both run-prefixed guilds' license fixtures are swept independently.

scenarios.promise: Dependency failure fails safe on both sides: with the license server down, an already-validated device rides the bounded offline window while a never-validated device is refused; a server-side lookup RPC failure returns a fail-closed 500 with no partial session writes.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The cached device reports offline_grace until the window ends, then offline_grace_expired; the fresh device gets network_error with no entitlement; the RPC-failure response is valid:false with a generic error and no session row.

assertions.expectedObservation: Guild access tied to entitlement does not expand during the outage.
No session or validation rows are written during the failed-RPC path beyond the error log.
The outage window shows logged network errors and the lookup failure event.
The owner is notified of the server-side lookup failure.
Offline and unreachable messages stay calm, branded, and actionable.
Repeated failing calls during the outage do not corrupt the cache or duplicate sessions on recovery.
Outage-simulation fixtures are fully removed after the run.

scenarios.promise: Transient failures converge: a validation that fails with a transient network fault or a 429 succeeds on retry, ending with exactly one active session for the device and correct honoring of Retry-After.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: After backoff the retried validate() returns valid with the same single session for that fingerprint; the rate-limited call retried too early is refused again, and after the window it succeeds; no duplicate sessions exist.

assertions.expectedObservation: The customer's guild standing is unchanged throughout the retry cycle.
Exactly one active session row exists for the fingerprint after convergence.
Failed, rate-limited, and successful attempts are each logged distinctly.
Converged retries raise no owner alert.
The rate-limit message states the wait plainly in the branded voice.
The converged end state equals a single clean validation.
Retry-test fixtures are swept with the run.

scenarios.promise: Replay grants nothing twice: identical validate, heartbeat, and deactivate requests replayed against the API create no duplicate sessions, consume no extra device slots, double no entitlements, and never mint anything in the play-money game economy.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Replayed validate reuses the existing session; replayed heartbeat only refreshes last_seen; replayed deactivate on an inactive session is a harmless no-op; slot accounting and key status are byte-identical to the single-execution baseline, and no game-economy row changed.

assertions.expectedObservation: No duplicate role grants or game-currency effects appear in the test guild from replays.
Session and slot counts match the no-replay baseline exactly.
Replayed requests are logged without inflating grant or status-change history.
Replays produce no duplicate notifications.
Replay responses reuse the standard branded templates without duplication artifacts.
The end state is provably identical to single execution across keys, sessions, and validations.
Replay fixtures are removed; the validation log of the replays persists as audit.

scenarios.promise: State survives a full stack restart: keys, sessions, and product config persist in Supabase; a customer app restarting mid-session revalidates into its existing session rather than consuming a fresh device slot.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: After dashboard restart, admin session listings and portal views match pre-restart state; the restarted SDK's validate() reoccupies the same fingerprint's session; heartbeat cadence resumes at the configured interval.

assertions.expectedObservation: Entitlement-driven guild behavior is continuous across the restart.
Persisted license rows retain their guild scoping and protections after restart.
Pre-restart validation history remains intact and ordered.
A clean restart raises no false license alerts.
Branded license surfaces render identically after restart.
Restart-triggered revalidation does not double-occupy device slots.
Restart-test fixtures are swept normally after the run.

scenarios.promise: Concurrency is safe at the limit: two new devices validating simultaneously for the last free slot resolve atomically — exactly one wins the slot and the other receives the device-limit rejection, with no over-allocation.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The FOR-UPDATE device registration RPC serializes the race; active session count never exceeds max-devices at any instant; the loser gets the branded limit message pointing at the reset path.

assertions.expectedObservation: Only the winning device's app reports activation to the customer.
Session rows never exceed the configured device cap, even transiently.
Both racing attempts are logged: one success, one device_limit rejection.
The routine race outcome raises no owner alert.
The losing device's message is the standard branded limit template.
Re-running the race yields the same single-winner invariant every time.
Both racers' fixtures are swept after the run.

scenarios.promise: Guild isolation is total: an identical product and key setup in a second run-prefixed guild shares nothing — validations, sessions, configs, and admin views for guild A never surface guild B data and vice versa.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Each guild's keys validate only against its own products; owner A's key lookups, session lists, and revocations cannot touch guild B rows; per-guild rate-limit and log records stay separate.

assertions.expectedObservation: License-gated behavior in each test guild reflects only that guild's entitlements.
Cross-guild queries return zero rows in both directions.
Validation logs carry the correct guild-scoped product for every attempt.
Each owner receives only their own guild's license notices.
Each guild's license messages use that guild's own brand configuration.
Replays in guild A cause no observable change in guild B.
Both guilds' run-prefixed license fixtures are swept independently and completely.

scenarios.promise: Run-prefixed license resources are fully cleaned: test customers, products, keys, sessions, and portal tokens created by the run are removed or anonymized, while validation-log audit rows persist under anonymize-over-delete.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: A post-run sweep finds zero run-prefixed license rows or active test sessions; the validation log retains anonymized rows documenting the run; a second sweep pass finds nothing.

assertions.expectedObservation: No run-prefixed license artifacts remain visible in either test guild.
Swept tables contain no run-prefixed rows; RLS policies are unchanged by cleanup.
Anonymized validation-log rows for the run persist and remain queryable.
A cleanup summary is available without alert noise.
Cleanup leaves owner branding configuration untouched.
Running the sweep twice is safe and idempotent.
Every created license resource is matched to a deletion or anonymization in the sweep report.
